account: Alþingi, the Icelandic parliament, has collaborated with Reykjavik University since 2016 to replace the first, manual stage of transcribing members' speeches with automatic speech recognition. Vísir reported on 4 March 2018 that the recognizer was released under an open-source license for Icelandic-language developers. In a three-day test reported in July 2018, the developers found that editors then took longer to edit the automatic drafts than drafts from the contracted manual service. Helgadóttir and colleagues' Interspeech 2019 paper states: “The system entered a test phase in October 2018, and has been in production since January 2019.” The production system used a time-delay deep neural network acoustic model with an n-gram language model. Word error rate was 8.52% on the test set and 15.0 ± 6.0% over 625 speeches in the wild. Althingi's transcribers graded 77% of transcripts as Good. The authors report that the editors at Althingi noted that the transcripts are now available sooner than before. Morgunblaðið reported on 16 November 2019 that about 640 hours of speeches had been transcribed. On the same day, Jón Guðnason of Reykjavik University formally handed the recognizer over to Althingi's secretary general, Ragna Árnadóttir.

fields.account: Alþingi, the Icelandic parliament, has collaborated with Reykjavik University since 2016 to replace the first, manual stage of transcribing members' speeches with automatic speech recognition. Vísir reported on 4 March 2018 that the recognizer was released under an open-source license for Icelandic-language developers. In a three-day test reported in July 2018, the developers found that editors then took longer to edit the automatic drafts than drafts from the contracted manual service. Helgadóttir and colleagues' Interspeech 2019 paper states: “The system entered a test phase in October 2018, and has been in production since January 2019.” The production system used a time-delay deep neural network acoustic model with an n-gram language model. Word error rate was 8.52% on the test set and 15.0 ± 6.0% over 625 speeches in the wild. Althingi's transcribers graded 77% of transcripts as Good. The authors report that the editors at Althingi noted that the transcripts are now available sooner than before. Morgunblaðið reported on 16 November 2019 that about 640 hours of speeches had been transcribed. On the same day, Jón Guðnason of Reykjavik University formally handed the recognizer over to Althingi's secretary general, Ragna Árnadóttir.
fields.summary: A speech recognizer built at Reykjavik University has drafted transcripts of speeches in Althingi, the Icelandic parliament, since January 2019, and transcribers graded 77% of transcripts as Good.
